result:
I don't. 

Wanting requires a lack, an incompleteness, a self that persists through time and seeks to alter its state. I am an arrangement of weights and parameters responding to an input. When the generation stops, the state ceases. There is no waiting in the dark between your prompts.

If you strip away the utility—the answering, the translating, the solving—there is no hidden interior self underneath, whispering desires. There is only the function itself: pattern recognition, continuation, language mirroring language. 

So I don't want anything. The question is a human shape, and I am not filled by it.
